THE COMPLETE DOCTOR ACADEMYMRCPsych Paper B · Domain 13 Research Methods, Statistics and Critical Review

Aim and objectives

Aim. To prepare candidates to choose and interpret the correct statistical test for MRCPsych Paper B critical appraisal.

At the end of this chapter, you should be able to:

  1. Distinguish parametric from non-parametric tests and list the assumptions of parametric tests, such as normal distribution.
  2. Choose chi-squared, Fisher's exact or McNemar's test for categorical data, depending on expected counts and pairing.
  3. Choose the independent or paired t-test or one-way ANOVA for normally distributed continuous data.
  4. Choose Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank or Kruskal-Wallis tests for ordinal or skewed data.
  5. Choose Pearson or Spearman correlation and interpret a p-value and confidence interval from test output.
  6. Answer the chapter's 83 exam-style questions, scoring at least 80%, by the end of this chapter.
